blocks.text: This chapter argues that the love is misplaced: past a point, every extra percent of utilization buys a disproportionate amount of waiting.
Below 70 percent the line is almost flat; past 80 it turns into a wall.
Utilization is only half the story; the other half is variability.
If waiting is the price of busyness, slack is not waste. It is capacity held in reserve for the work you cannot predict.
Nobody ever got a promotion for the fire that didn't start.
blocks.attribution: A plant manager interviewed by Ines Okafor
